title: Listening with Language Models: Using LLMs to Collect and Interpret Classroom Feedback
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether large language model (LLM)-powered chatbots can improve the classroom feedback process compared with traditional end-of-quarter surveys. The authors argue that standard surveys are often too delayed, generic, and poorly aligned with instructors’ needs, making them weak tools for obtaining actionable teaching feedback.

To address this, the paper presents a three-part system: PromptDesigner for instructors to co-design course-specific feedback prompts, FeedbackCollector for students to provide conversational feedback through a GPT-4-powered chatbot, and FeedbackAnalyzer for instructors to review anonymized responses and AI-generated summaries. Instructors could upload syllabi, choose topics such as assignment clarity or lecture engagement, and revise prompts over the quarter. Students interacted asynchronously through a secure platform, and faculty later reviewed dashboards summarizing themes from the conversations.

The system was piloted in two graduate courses at the University of California, Santa Cruz—Game Data Science and Ethics in HCI—with one instructor and 40 students. The study used co-design sessions, a mid-quarter deployment of the chatbot, and post-course semi-structured interviews with six students and the instructor. The results suggest that the LLM-based system produced richer, more contextual, and more timely feedback than standard surveys, helped instructors make mid-course adjustments, and was generally appreciated by students for its conversational style. However, students also raised concerns about anonymity and wanted stronger privacy reassurance in the interface.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: An OpenAI GPT-based large language model chatbot used for conversational interaction, text generation, and summarization/analysis tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as the GPT-4-powered student-facing FeedbackCollector chatbot to gather classroom feedback conversationally, and within FeedbackAnalyzer to generate summaries of anonymized student responses.

findings.finding_summary: In two graduate courses (n=40 total students), the LLM-based feedback system was reported to be quicker and more efficient than the university’s standard end-of-quarter survey. The instructor said it took about five minutes and yielded 23 feedback responses, substantially more than they typically received through SETS; students also found the conversational format engaging.
findings.measure: Instructor-reported efficiency and response volume; student interview feedback about engagement compared with standard surveys
findings.sample_size: n=40 (pilot classes); n=6 student interviews + 1 instructor interview

quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative pilot study with semi-structured interviews and a small case-study deployment, not a controlled trial. It provides useful implementation insight but limited causal evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports clear practical benefits in timeliness, response volume, and perceived usefulness, but no quantitative effect size is reported. Impact is promising yet currently unclear in magnitude.
